t.6.105.1: Then King Vaiśravaṇa, and Yama, the tormentor of enemies, and great Indra, the thousand-eyed, and Varuṇa, scorcher of foes, came forth.
t.6.105.2: The glorious three-eyed Mahādeva, whose banner bears the bull, and Brahmā, the creator of the whole world and foremost among the knowers of brahman, came there.
t.6.105.3: All of these, having assembled together in aerial chariots resplendent like the sun, came to the city of Laṅkā and approached Rāghava.
t.6.105.4: Then the foremost of the thirty gods, raising their mighty arms adorned with ornaments on their hands, spoke to Rāghava, who stood before them with joined palms.
t.6.105.5: You are the creator of the whole world, the foremost, the best among those endowed with knowledge; how can you disregard Sītā as she falls into the fire? How do you not recognize yourself as the foremost of the hosts of gods?
t.6.105.6: Formerly you were Ṛtadhāman, the Vasu, and the Prajāpati of the Vasus; for you are the first creator of the three worlds, the self-existent lord.
t.6.105.7: Among the Rudras you are the eighth Rudra, and among the Sādhyas the fifth; the two Aśvins are your ears, and the moon and the sun are your eyes.
t.6.105.8: You are seen at the end and at the beginning of the worlds, O scorcher of foes, and yet you disregard Vaidehī like an ordinary mortal.
t.6.105.9: Thus addressed by those guardians of the worlds, Rāghava, lord of the world, Rāma, foremost among the upholders of dharma, spoke to the best of the gods.
t.6.105.10: I consider myself a human being, Rāma, the son of Daśaratha. Who I am, to whom I belong, and from where I have come, let the Blessed One tell me that.
t.6.105.11: To Kākutstha, who was speaking thus, Brahmā, foremost among the knowers of brahman, said: "Hear from me the truth, O Rāma, you whose valor is true."
t.6.105.12: You are the lord Nārāyaṇa, glorious and all-pervading, who bears the discus as his weapon. You are the one-horned Boar, the conqueror of foes past and future.
t.6.105.13: O Rāghava, you are the imperishable, the true Brahman, present in the middle and at the end. You are the supreme dharma of the worlds, Viṣvaksena, the four-armed one.
t.6.105.14: You are the wielder of the Śārṅga bow, Hṛṣīkeśa, the Puruṣa, the Supreme Person, the unconquered one, the bearer of the sword, Viṣṇu, and indeed Kṛṣṇa of mighty strength.
t.6.105.16: You are Indrakarman, the great Indra, Padmanābha, the one who brings an end to battle; the divine great sages call you the refuge and the one worthy of giving shelter.
t.6.105.15: You are the leader of armies and the chief of the people; you are intellect, strength, forbearance and self-restraint. You are the origin and also the dissolution; you are Upendra and Madhusūdana.
t.6.105.17: You are the thousand-horned one whose very self is the Veda, the hundred-tongued great bull; you are the sacrifice, you are the exclamation vaṣaṭ, you are the sacred syllable Om, O scorcher of foes.
t.6.105.18: They know neither your origin nor your end, nor who you are. You are seen in all beings, in brāhmaṇas and in cows.
t.6.105.20: You sustain all beings and the earth together with its mountains; at the end of the earth, in the waters, you are seen as the great serpent.
t.6.105.19: In all the directions, in the sky, on the mountains and in the forests, you are the glorious one with a thousand feet and a hundred heads, the upholder of thousands.
t.6.105.21: O Rāma, you sustain the three worlds with their gods, gandharvas and dānavas; I am your heart, O Rāma, and the goddess Sarasvatī is your tongue.
t.6.105.22: O Lord, the gods were fashioned by Brahmā as the hairs upon your limbs. The closing of your eyes became the night, and the opening of your eyes became the day.
t.6.105.23: The Vedas became your purificatory rites; there is nothing that exists without you. The whole universe is your body, and the surface of the earth is your steadfastness.
t.6.105.24: Your anger is Agni and your grace is Soma, O you who bear the mark of the Śrīvatsa. In ancient times the three worlds were traversed by you with three strides.
t.6.105.25: Having bound Bali, the great asura, you made great Indra king. Sītā is Lakṣmī, and you are Viṣṇu, the god Kṛṣṇa, Prajāpati.
t.6.105.26: For the slaying of Rāvaṇa you entered here into a human body; so this task of ours has been accomplished by you, O best among the upholders of dharma.
t.6.105.27: Rāvaṇa is slain, O Rāma; now, rejoicing, ascend to heaven. Unfailing are your strength and valour, and unfailing is your prowess.
t.6.105.28: Those men who are devoted to you will never be fruitless; those who are steadfastly devoted to you, the ancient god, the supreme Person, and those men who sing your praises, will never meet with defeat.
